claims.text: Disclosed pay structure - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) states that financial advisor compensation and benefits expense rose because of increases in revenues on which commissions are earned. It also states that variable compensation "expands and contracts in relation to the Partnership's profitability and margin earned", is paid to associates as bonuses and profit sharing, and is "a key component of the Firm's performance-based compensation model".

Disclosed pay structure - Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K segment note says financial advisor bonuses are determined by the overall Partnership's profitability as well as the performance of individual financial advisors.

Disclosed pay structure - Edward Jones: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-03-27) says the Program Fee, assets under care and Reserve Line Advance balances impact most financial advisors' bonus eligibility and amount, and may affect eligibility for limited partnership Profits Interest. It also says most advisors are eligible for a Travel Award Program based on new and existing assets under care. The firm itself flags both as conflicts of interest.

Disclosed pay structure - Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) attributes the rise in Wealth Management compensation to "an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue". The excerpts do not give the formula's rates.

Disclosed pay structure - Schwab: not found in the evidence provided. The Schwab chunks describe pay only at the employee-wide level (see adjacent) and nothing specific to advisor compensation structure. Suggested source: Schwab proxy statement or recruiting materials.

Disclosed pay structure - Raymond James: Its financial advisor compensation expense is reported in two lines, "Commissions, benefits and other compensation" and "Recruiting and retention-related compensation". The footnote says the latter includes cash and equity awards issued for recruiting, as retention for existing advisors, or with acquisitions, expensed over the requisite service period (typically between 5 and 10 years) (press release published 2026-07-22).

Disclosed pay structure - Raymond James: Its advisory brochure (published 2026-09-14) says the Institutional Account Participation Program pays referral fees to financial advisors for referring institutional clients to Raymond James Investment Management, as a percentage of the management fee earned.

Disclosed pay structure - Merrill: Its advisory program brochure (published 2026-10-30) states that Merrill determines compensation paid to its Advisors "on the same basis for all Program assets without regard to the amount of compensation we or our Affiliates receive", and that advisors receive no additional compensation from certain Third-Party Firm arrangements.

Published payout rates - Raymond James: Raymond James's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) lists a Corporate RIA model with an "81% to 90% payout" (minimum 3 years' experience and $50 million in assets under advisement). For the Bank & Credit Union model it describes only "a competitive compensation package from the financial institution". For RIA & Custody Services it says compensation is determined with the RIA or broker/dealer.

Recent change and trend - Edward Jones (oldest to newest): The 2025 10-K reports financial advisor compensation and benefits up 12% to $6,969 in 2025, and variable compensation up 11% to $2,710 on branch and Firm profitability. The Q1 2026 10-Q (published 2026-05-07) reports advisor compensation up 13% to $1,875 and variable compensation up 22% to $748. The Q2 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) reports advisor compensation up 18% to $2,001 for the quarter and up 16% to $3,876 for the first half, and variable compensation up 33% to $780 and up 27% to $1,528. Each filing attributes the advisor compensation rise to revenues on which commissions are earned.

Recent change and trend - Morgan Stanley (oldest to newest): On the 4Q25 call (published 2026-01-15) a company representative said the firm will transition all DCP economic hedges to derivative instruments, "increase the cash component of our advisor compensation" and make these changes "to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings". The representative added that there will be some transitional costs, and that the changes "support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program".

Recent change and trend - Morgan Stanley: The Q2 2026 supplement (published 2026-07-15) says that from Q1 2026 Wealth Management DCP hedges were primarily moved to derivative instruments, and that the firm no longer presents non-GAAP measures excluding DCP. The Q2 2026 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) says Wealth Management compensation and benefits rose "primarily as a result of an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenues".

Recent change and trend - Schwab: advisor-specific compensation changes or expense figures were not found in the evidence provided. Suggested source: Schwab 10-K/10-Q compensation and benefits disclosure or proxy statement.

Recent change and trend - Raymond James (oldest to newest): On the 3Q25 call (published 2025-10-22) the CFO said fiscal 2025 adjusted compensation expense included $355 million of amortization of transition assistance for recruited advisors and retention awards to existing advisors, up approximately 11% on fiscal 2024. On the 4Q25 call (published 2026-01-28) the CFO said the firm began presenting recruiting and retention-related compensation in the PCG segment each period because these costs rose as a direct result of its recruiting successes.

Recent change and trend - Raymond James: The release for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (published 2026-07-22) shows PCG total financial advisor compensation of $1,683 million for the quarter, up 19% from a year earlier. That is made up of $1,566 million of commissions, benefits and other compensation and $117 million of recruiting and retention-related compensation, up 21%. For nine months it shows $4,632 million of commissions, benefits and other compensation and $335 million of recruiting and retention-related compensation (up 22%), totalling $4,967 million.
Raymond James: Headline payout ranges are published (company recruiting page, as of 2026-04-21); the full payout grid is not public.

adjacent.text: Morgan Stanley's 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) states that firm-wide compensation and benefits expense includes base salaries and fixed allowances, formulaic programs, discretionary incentive compensation, amortization of deferred cash and equity awards, changes in the fair value of referenced notional DCP investments, carried interest, severance and other items. It also reports firm-wide Compensation and benefits expenses of $29,216 million in 2025, up 12%.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: Schwab's 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) says its employee compensation package includes base pay, performance-based incentive pay, equity awards and recognition awards. On the 3Q26 call (published 2026-10-15) the CFO said the year-over-year rise in adjusted expenses reflected higher volume-related costs, including performance-based compensation.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: Schwab's investor day deck (published 2026-05-14) says independent Schwab Advisor Network advisors "pay fees to Schwab in connection with referrals".
adjacent.differs_because: This describes fees independent advisors pay Schwab; it is not how Schwab pays its own advisors.
